framework_version_u_reason: (U) the serving plan names vLLM but the campaign has not pinned a build; established by the first INFO banner line of the engine log, or `python -m vllm --version` inside the serving container, once the engine is installed on the tray.
container_digest_u_reason: (U) the serving image for this campaign has not been chosen yet; established by `docker inspect --format={{.RepoDigests}}` or the enroot image manifest once the container exists.
max_model_len_u_reason: (U) the launch command is not frozen and no --max-model-len value has been decided; established by the launch script and the engine config dump at startup, with the checkpoint's native 128,000 as the ceiling.
memory_utilization_u_reason: (U) the effective gpu_memory_utilization is only known after the engine boots and profiles, and the serving plan declares no cap; established by the engine's memory-profiling log lines and reconciled with calibrate_memory_utilization against the reported KV pool.
prefix_caching_u_reason: (U) the serving plan is silent on it and the gemma campaign's on was inherited from its own text campaign, a comparability argument this campaign does not have; established by reading the final launch command.
kv_cache_offload_u_reason: (U) the serving plan does not state it; established by the launch command and the engine config log once the command is frozen.
chunked_prefill_u_reason: (U) the serving plan does not state it and the engine version that would fix the default is itself not pinned; established by the launch command and config dump at startup.
engine_reported_kv_cache_tokens_u_reason: (U) the engine has not booted on this tray with these weights; established by the startup log line reporting the GPU KV cache size in tokens and GiB once vLLM is launched.
cold_start_to_ready_s_u_reason: (U) the engine has not been started; measured from the first banner line to the last route-registration line in the server log, the same method the gemma campaign used.

media_preprocessing.video_sampling_fps_u_reason: (U) the checkpoint's preprocessor declares tokens_per_second 2 for video with temporal_patch_size 2, which implies about 1 frame per second delivered, but whether the to-be-pinned vLLM build honours that relation has not been checked; established by reading the video processor of the installed engine, and this campaign sends no video.
media_preprocessing.video_max_frames_u_reason: (U) the not-yet-installed engine's frame cap has not been checked; established by its video processor config or a probing request, and this campaign sends no video regardless.

notes.image_pixel_budget_px: 1,003,520 pixels, set at launch through --mm-processor-kwargs with max_pixels 1,003,520 and min_pixels 3,136 in the same flag, so no client can move it. Where the gemma bundle declared a selectable soft-token tier, this is a pixel budget: the model is dynamic-resolution, an image costs approximately ceil(height/28) x ceil(width/28) tokens, and the budget is exactly 1,280 of those 28 x 28 merged cells, which is the 1,280-token ceiling on per-image cost. Above the budget the preprocessor downscales the image to fit rather than rejecting, so this is the cap that binds silently: what the model sees of a 2352 x 1695 scan is that scan at whatever resolution fits 1,003,520 pixels, and nothing in the token counts reveals the rescale. Below min_pixels 3,136 a small image is upscaled to the floor.
notes.mm_processor_cache_gb: Set to 0 on purpose, for the same reason the gemma campaign disabled it: the ladder draws with replacement from a 3,256-record corpus and a 120 s window at concurrency 128 issues more requests than the corpus has records, so a cache would serve repeats that the workload's unique-media-prefix policy says cannot happen. With the cache off every request pays host-side decode and patchify, no image is preprocessed twice, and the declared policy is true.
notes.per_request_override_supported: Declared false as the schema's default assumption and not exercised in this campaign. The cap is applied at launch, not per request, so no per-request mm_processor_kwargs a client could send is part of this declaration; on the gemma evidence a probe of this kind can terminate the server, so the test is queued for after the ladder's bundle is pulled.

notes.limit_mm_per_prompt_is_a_launch_flag_the: The engine will be launched with a per-prompt image limit admitting at least 8 images, because this corpus averages 4.19 images per record and its tail runs longer than that, while the engine default of 1 would reject those requests with HTTP 400. A rejected request is not a slow request, it returns in milliseconds, so an under-set limit inflates throughput and empties the media out of a media benchmark while every SLO gate still passes; media_arrival_check catches it after the fact and the flag is what stops it from firing. ASCEP has no field for the per-modality admission limit, so as in the gemma bundle it is recorded here in prose and an operator reproducing this bundle has to read the note.
